summary: Read desired declarations, selected declaration tokens and cheap actual summaries together with fractal subject desired --json [--all | SUBJECT...] [--kind K]. The CLI follows bounded desired GET pages, collecting one final array without status reduction or cold card folds.

replay.detail: No graph replay or new projection. The desired(kind, subject) index is local query acceleration, not authoritative schema or replay state.

schema.detail: Adds GET /v1/desired?subject=ID&subject=ID&kind=K&limit=N&cursor=TOKEN. Repeated URL-encoded subject names are optional (omission selects all); kind and cursor are optional. More than 1,000 supplied names returns desired-batch-limit. Page limit defaults to 1,000, with maximum 1,000; zero or over-limit values return HTTP 422 desired-page-limit. Each page is {items: DesiredBatchItem[], next_cursor: string|null, store_index: u64}. Items flatten DesiredSubject with nullable desired_token and optional extensible actual, including published mission definitions. This raw route is outside generated client-v0 schemas.

rules.detail: No checkpoint or declaration selection rule changes.

compatibility.detail: The desired collection GET inherits existing read.projections authorization, deadlines and read admission, including paired-device refusal without that scope, and works during fleet drain. Per-subject desired reads, subject cards, sparse summary and digest semantics are unchanged. Missing summary fields require fetching the card, not interpreting them as negative observations.

downtime.detail: Normal startup automatically creates the desired(kind, subject) query index on existing desired rows before serving reads. This one-time index build adds startup work proportional to existing desired declarations; no offline migration or planned downtime is required.

manual.detail: No manual or offline index-installation step; ordinary store startup installs the index.

recovery.detail: Opaque cursors bind store origin, pinned read cut, projection progress for every family read, selection filters, page limit and last subject. Continuations must preserve filters and limit and validate the same current cut and projection progress; a changed cut or projection progress returns typed desired-cursor-expired, including backlog projection advances without new claims. There is no historical snapshot, pagination cache, silent restart or retry. The CLI follows cursors with unchanged filters and limit 1,000, prints one final array only on complete success, and fails without partial stdout on cursor invalidation. Older daemons lack the collection route; existing per-subject reads remain available.
